provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Puts up representative options and leaves the pick to the hearer, pairing dictionary-form verbs or plain nouns: 電話するなりメールするなり, 映画なり温泉なり. The sibling entry is the 'as soon as' sense, one dictionary-form verb plus なり reporting what someone did the instant something happened (顔を見るなり泣き出した). It usually leads into a suggestion, request, or permission, and sounds curt toward a superior.

examples.ruby: 余[あま]った野菜[やさい]は煮[に]るなり焼[や]くなり好[す]きにして。
examples.english: Do whatever you like with the leftover vegetables — simmer them, grill them, your call.

examples.ruby: 週末[しゅうまつ]は映画[えいが]なり温泉[おんせん]なりで気分[きぶん]を変[か]えよう。
examples.english: Let's change things up this weekend with a movie or a hot spring or something.

examples.ruby: 心配[しんぱい]なら見[み]に来[く]るなり電話[でんわ]するなりしてよ。
examples.english: If you're worried, come see for yourself or give me a call — either one.

patterns.usage_note: Joins two or more nouns as representative samples of a longer set: 鍵や財布 means keys, a wallet, and other things besides. A sibling lane is the literary 〜や after a dictionary-form verb, marking one event following instantly on another (見るや). It joins nouns only, and the list is often closed with など; と instead presents the list as complete.

examples.ruby: 机[つくえ]の上[うえ]に鍵[かぎ]や財布[さいふ]が置[お]いてある。
examples.english: There are keys, a wallet, and things like that sitting on the desk.

examples.ruby: 休[やす]みの日[ひ]は洗濯[せんたく]や掃除[そうじ]であっという間[ま]だ。
examples.english: My days off fly by doing laundry, cleaning, and the rest of it.

examples.ruby: 公園[こうえん]には桜[さくら]や銀杏[いちょう]の木[き]が多[おお]い。
examples.english: The park has plenty of cherry and ginkgo trees, among others.

patterns.usage_note: Cites representative examples: とか follows each item listed and marks the list as partial (カレーとかパスタとか, 走るとか出かけるとか). The sibling lane is the sentence-final hearsay とか, relaying what you heard without vouching for it (会社を辞めるとか). It attaches more freely than や, taking nouns, plain-form verbs, i-adjectives, and past た, and it is usually avoided in formal writing as too vague.

examples.ruby: 暇[ひま]な日[ひ]は走[はし]るとか出[で]かけるとかしている。
examples.english: On free days I go running, or head out somewhere, that kind of thing.

examples.ruby: 甘[あま]いとか酸[す]っぱいとか、感想[かんそう]がばらばらだ。
examples.english: Sweet, sour — everyone described it differently.

examples.ruby: 昼[ひる]はカレーとかパスタとかでいいよ。
examples.english: Curry, pasta, whatever — anything's fine for lunch.

glosses: … and … and what have you (listing gripes)
patterns.usage_note: だの lists two or more examples with the speaker's irritation attached: the items are usually complaints, excuses, or a jumble the speaker is fed up with (狭いだの暗いだの), rarely a neutral description. The plain past ending た/だ is a different item (読んだ). Spoken, it attaches to nouns, plain verbs, i-adjectives and な-adjectives much as とか does, but とか is the neutral choice.

examples.ruby: 部屋[へや]が狭[せま]いだの暗[くら]いだのと注文[ちゅうもん]が多[おお]い。
examples.english: The room's too small, it's too dark — he's endlessly demanding.

examples.ruby: 姉[あね]は荷物[にもつ]が重[おも]いだの靴[くつ]が痛[いた]いだのと止[と]まってばかりだ。
examples.english: My sister keeps stopping — the bag's too heavy, her shoes hurt.

examples.ruby: 走[はし]るだの泳[およ]ぐだの言[い]うだけで、何[なに]もしない。
examples.english: He goes on about running and swimming and whatnot, and never does any of it.

patterns.usage_note: Piles up items to show that the situation is chaotic or the feelings mixed (引っ越しやら手続きやら, 嬉しいやら恥ずかしいやら). だの points its irritation at someone, while やら usually leaves the speaker simply swamped. Beyond the nouns and i-adjectives this entry licenses, plain-form verbs also take it (泣くやら笑うやら), and it appears in written narration as well as speech.

examples.ruby: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しやら手続[てつづ]きやらで目[め]が回[まわ]りそうだ。
examples.english: Between the move and all the paperwork, my head is spinning.

examples.ruby: 嬉[うれ]しいやら恥[は]ずかしいやらで、顔[かお]が赤[あか]くなった。
examples.english: Half delighted, half mortified, I went red in the face.

examples.ruby: 鞄[かばん]の中[なか]はレシートやら飴[あめ]やらでぐちゃぐちゃだ。
examples.english: My bag is a disaster — receipts, loose candy, you name it.
